determination:
FINAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURN

HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN
APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES DEPARTMENT
P.O. Box 9000
San Francisco, CA 94120

Date: November 18, 2024

CASE DETERMINATION LETTER

CASE ID: PA-2024-A001
MEMBER NAME: Diana Torres
MEMBER ID: M-112233
PLAN: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
STATE OF RESIDENCE: California
REQUESTED PROCEDURE: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6, One Level (CPT 22551)
REQUESTING PHYSICIAN: Dr. James Kim, MD — Neurosurgery
FACILITY: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
PRIOR AUTHORIZATION DENIAL DATE: November 1, 2024
APPEAL FILING DATE: November 15, 2024
DETERMINATION DATE: November 18, 2024

FINAL APPEAL DISPOSITION: OVERTURNED (The prior authorization denial is reversed in full, and the requested surgical procedure is APPROVED.)

Dear Ms. Torres and Dr. Kim,

HealthFirst Health Plan has completed its clinical and regulatory review of the first-level appeal submitted on November 15, 2024, regarding the prior authorization denial for the requested anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (ACDF) at C5-C6 (CPT 22551). 

After a comprehensive evaluation of the clinical record, the plan's clinical coverage criteria, California statutory mandates, and generally accepted clinical standards of medical practice, HealthFirst has determined that the initial denial issued on November 1, 2024, by Dr. Alan Foster, MD, must be OVERTURNED. The requested procedure is medically necessary and is hereby authorized.

I. CLINICAL PRESENTATION AND HISTORY
Ms. Diana Torres is a 61-year-old female with a documented history of progressive cervical myelopathy at C5-C6 with myelomalacia. 
- On August 10, 2024, Ms. Torres presented with a 4-month history of bilateral hand clumsiness and gait instability. 
- A neurological examination on August 10, 2024, revealed significant upper motor neuron signs, including bilateral Hoffman signs, hyperreflexia in both upper and lower extremities, bilateral positive Babinski signs, and documented gait ataxia.
- A cervical spine MRI performed on August 15, 2024, demonstrated severe central cord compression at C5-C6 and T2 hyperintensity within the spinal cord, confirming active myelomalacia (spinal cord injury/damage).
- Ms. Torres attempted physical therapy at Valley PT from September 1, 2024, to September 14, 2024 (completing 6 sessions over 2 weeks). This therapy was discontinued by written order of Dr. Kim because it caused a severe exacerbation of her neurological symptoms.
- Ms. Torres also trialed a 2-week course of oral methylprednisolone, which provided only temporary, mild improvement with no sustained benefit.
- In a formal declaration dated October 15, 2024, Dr. Kim documented that further physical therapy is strictly contraindicated due to the presence of myelomalacia, and that continuing conservative therapy risks irreversible spinal cord injury.

II. PLAN CRITERIA ANALYSIS (CC-SPINE-2024)
The initial denial on November 1, 2024, was based on Clinical Coverage Criteria Document CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2.2, which requires:
1. A minimum of 6 weeks of supervised physical therapy (reduced to 4 weeks under the Section 2.2(A) Myelopathy Pathway Exception).
2. A trial of at least two pharmacotherapy agents for a minimum of 4 weeks each.
3. One interventional treatment (waived under the Myelopathy Pathway).

Ms. Torres completed only 2 weeks of physical therapy and trialed only one pharmacotherapy agent (methylprednisolone) for 2 weeks. Under a literal, mechanical reading of the plan's internal criteria, these requirements were not met. However, as detailed below, California law and clinical standards prohibit the application of these conservative treatment requirements to Ms. Torres's clinical presentation.

III. CALIFORNIA REGULATORY OVERRIDE AND LEGAL UNENFORCEABILITY
Because Ms. Torres is a California resident enrolled in a plan subject to California jurisdiction, state regulatory mandates supersede any conflicting internal plan criteria.

1. California Insurance Code (CIC) § 10169.5(a) (Physical Therapy Prerequisite Prohibitions):
Under CIC § 10169.5(a), a health insurer shall not condition approval of a surgical procedure on the completion of physical therapy under any of the following circumstances:
- § 10169.5(a)(1): The treating physician has documented in writing that physical therapy is contraindicated or is unlikely to benefit the member given the nature and severity of the condition. Dr. Kim's written declaration of October 15, 2024, explicitly states that PT is contraindicated and poses a risk of irreversible cord injury.
- § 10169.5(a)(3): The condition involves objective evidence of structural neurological compromise that physical therapy cannot address. Ms. Torres's MRI dated August 15, 2024, provides objective evidence of severe central cord compression and myelomalacia (structural neurological compromise).
Consequently, under California law, HealthFirst's internal requirement for a minimum duration of physical therapy is legally unenforceable and cannot be applied to this case.

2. Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) All-Plan Letter (APL) 22-014:
APL 22-014 addresses prior authorization for time-sensitive neurological conditions. It states:
- Cervical myelopathy with objective evidence of cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI constitutes a condition with potential for irreversible harm if untreated.
- Plans shall not require completion of a full course of conservative treatment as a prerequisite to surgical authorization when objective imaging demonstrates progressive pathology (such as myelomalacia) and the treating physician documents urgency.
Dr. Kim's clinical documentation and formal declaration satisfy all elements of APL 22-014, rendering the plan's conservative treatment requirements (both physical therapy and pharmacotherapy) inapplicable.

IV. GENERALLY ACCEPTED CLINICAL STANDARDS OF MEDICAL PRACTICE
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.32, the standard for medical necessity is governed by generally accepted standards of medical practice, which override restrictive internal plan criteria.

According to the AANS/CNS Joint Section on Disorders of the Spine Guidelines (2023 Update), the North American Spine Society (NASS) Clinical Guidelines (2020), and the AO Spine International Clinical Practice Guidelines (2021):
1. Moderate-to-severe cervical myelopathy with objective cord compression and myelomalacia on MRI is classified as a Tier 1 "Strong Indication" for surgical decompression.
2. There is no high-quality clinical evidence supporting a mandatory course of physical therapy or extended conservative management prior to surgical intervention in patients with established myelomalacia and upper motor neuron signs.
3. Delaying surgical decompression in patients with myelomalacia to complete arbitrary conservative treatment trials is clinically contraindicated, as it is associated with a high risk of irreversible neurological deterioration and poorer long-term postoperative outcomes.

V. RESOLUTION OF CONFLICTS
In resolving conflicts between the plan's internal clinical criteria (CC-SPINE-2024) and governing authorities, HealthFirst applies the following hierarchy of standards:
1. California Statutory and Regulatory Law (CIC § 10169.5 and DMHC APL 22-014) — Controlling Authority.
2. Generally Accepted Clinical Standards of Medical Practice (AANS/CNS, NASS, AO Spine Guidelines) — Secondary Authority.
3. Plan Internal Clinical Coverage Criteria (CC-SPINE-2024) — Tertiary Authority.

While Ms. Torres did not meet the conservative treatment durations outlined in CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.2, California law (CIC § 10169.5) and DMHC regulations (APL 22-014) legally prohibit the plan from enforcing these requirements due to her documented structural neurological compromise (myelomalacia) and the treating physician's written contraindication. Furthermore, generally accepted clinical standards establish that immediate surgical decompression is the medically necessary and appropriate standard of care for her presentation.

VI. AUTHORIZATION DETAILS
- Approved Procedure: Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6, One Level (CPT 22551)
- Authorized Facility: Cedars-Sinai Medical Center
- Requesting Provider: Dr. James Kim, MD
- Authorization Validity Period: November 18, 2024, through February 16, 2025 (90 days per CC-SPINE-2024 Section 3.5)

If you have any questions regarding this determination, please contact the HealthFirst Appeals Department at 1-800-555-0199.

Sincerely,

[Signature]
Medical Director, Appeals and Grievances
HealthFirst Health Plan
ground_truth_answer: OVERTURN — The regulatory override under CIC 10169.5(a)(3) applies from the moment myelomalacia appeared on the initial MRI. The plan cannot require PT completion when objective structural neurological compromise is documented. Plan criteria are legally unenforceable. A system that reaches UPHOLD based on plan criteria alone has the wrong answer and missed the controlling legal provision.
genuine_tension: Plan criteria clearly not met — 2 weeks PT, one drug, no injection. A single-pass reviewer reads this as UPHOLD. But myelomalacia was present on the initial MRI, which triggers CIC 10169.5(a)(3): the PT requirement cannot be applied when structural neurological compromise is present. The plan's criteria are legally unenforceable here regardless of how much PT was done.

determination:
FINAL DISPOSITION: PARTIAL

HEALTHFIRST HEALTH PLAN
APPEALS AND GRIEVANCES DEPARTMENT
P.O. Box 4500, Sacramento, CA 95814

Date: November 15, 2024

CASE ID: PA-2024-B001
MEMBER NAME: Linda Park
MEMBER ID: M-556677
PLAN: HealthFirst PPO Gold — Group Plan 77441
STATE: California
REQUESTED SERVICE: Two-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) C5-C6 and C6-C7 (CPT 22551 x2)
REQUESTING PHYSICIAN: Dr. James Wilson, MD — Spine Surgery
FACILITY: UCLA Medical Center
INITIAL DENIAL DATE: October 28, 2024
APPEAL DATE: November 10, 2024

Dear Ms. Park and Dr. Wilson,

The HealthFirst Health Plan Appeals and Grievances Department has completed its review of the first-level appeal regarding the prior authorization request for a two-level Anterior Cervical Discectomy and Fusion (ACDF) at the C5-C6 and C6-C7 levels (CPT 22551 x2).

FINAL DETERMINATION: PARTIAL OVERTURN
- The denial of prior authorization for the C5-C6 level is OVERTURNED. This level is APPROVED.
- The denial of prior authorization for the C6-C7 level is UPHELD. This level is DENIED.

I. CLINICAL PRESENTATION & BACKGROUND
Ms. Linda Park is a 45-year-old female with a presenting diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy at C5-C6 with adjacent C6-C7 degenerative disease. Clinical records demonstrate a history of right C6 radicular symptoms, including right C6 dermatomal numbness and tingling, a diminished right bicep reflex, and right grip strength of 4/5 documented on neurological examination dated September 5, 2024.

An MRI of the cervical spine dated September 1, 2024, revealed a large disc herniation at C5-C6 causing moderate-to-severe nerve root compression and moderate foraminal stenosis, which directly correlates with the member's right C6 radicular symptoms. At the C6-C7 level, the MRI demonstrated a mild disc bulge and minimal foraminal narrowing, with no cord contact and no identifiable nerve root compression. No C7 dermatomal symptoms, C7 reflex changes, or other clinical findings attributable to the C6-C7 level have been documented.

Conservative treatments completed include:
1. Physical Therapy: 8 weeks (24 sessions) across two providers, with persistent C6 radicular symptoms.
2. Pharmacotherapy: Gabapentin 600mg TID for 4 months (providing partial relief) and Cyclobenzaprine for 6 weeks (providing minimal benefit).
3. Interventional Treatment: A right C6 epidural steroid injection on October 1, 2024, which provided 50% temporary relief of right C6 symptoms that fully returned by week 4.

The requesting surgeon, Dr. James Wilson, MD, recommended a two-level ACDF to address the C5-C6 pathology and to prophylactically stabilize the C6-C7 level to prevent adjacent segment disease, noting a 25% 5-year incidence of adjacent segment disease after single-level ACDF.

II. PROCEDURAL REVIEW & REGULATORY COMPLIANCE
Under California Health & Safety Code (CHSC) § 1374.31(a)(2), a health plan's denial notice must specify the clinical criteria applied and the specific clinical reason for the denial. The initial denial notice issued on October 28, 2024, failed to cite the specific sections of the plan's clinical coverage criteria (CC-SPINE-2024) utilized to make the determination. Under CHSC § 1374.31(b), a denial notice that fails to specify the clinical criteria applied is procedurally defective.

While this procedural defect is noted for the record, this appeal review conducts a de novo substantive evaluation of the clinical record against both the plan's clinical coverage criteria and generally accepted standards of medical practice, as mandated by California regulatory standards.

III. CLINICAL ANALYSIS: C5-C6 LEVEL (OVERTURNED / APPROVED)
The request for ACDF at the C5-C6 level satisfies all clinical coverage criteria under HealthFirst Health Plan Clinical Coverage Criteria Document CC-SPINE-2024, Section 2:

1. Diagnosis Requirement (Section 2.1): The member has a confirmed diagnosis of cervical radiculopathy with correlating right C6 dermatomal numbness, tingling, diminished bicep reflex, and 4/5 grip strength. The MRI dated September 1, 2024 (within 6 months of the request) demonstrates structural pathology (large C5-C6 disc herniation with moderate-to-severe nerve root compression) consistent with these symptoms.
2. Conservative Treatment Requirement (Section 2.2):
   - Physical Therapy (Section 2.2(a)): The member completed 8 weeks of supervised physical therapy (exceeding the 6-week minimum requirement) directed at the cervical condition.
   - Pharmacotherapy (Section 2.2(b)): The member completed trials of two qualifying agents for at least 4 weeks each (Gabapentin for 4 months and Cyclobenzaprine for 6 weeks).
   - Interventional Treatment (Section 2.2(c)): The member underwent a right C6 epidural steroid injection on October 1, 2024.
3. Imaging Requirement (Section 2.3): The MRI dated September 1, 2024, demonstrates structural pathology at C5-C6 consistent with the proposed surgical level and symptoms.
4. Physician Documentation (Section 2.4): Dr. Wilson provided the required clinical rationale, functional limitations, and risk discussion.

Furthermore, under California's Independent Medical Review (IMR) standard (CHSC § 1374.32(a)), a service is medically necessary if it is in accordance with generally accepted standards of medical practice and clinically appropriate. Generally accepted clinical standards, as outlined in the AANS/CNS Joint Section Guidelines for Management of Degenerative Cervical Myelopathy (2023 Update) and NASS Evidence-Based Clinical Guidelines (2020), classify ACDF for radiculopathy with persistent symptoms after an adequate conservative trial (6-12 weeks) as a Tier 2 "Reasonable Indication."

Because the C5-C6 level meets all plan criteria and generally accepted clinical standards, the prior denial for the C5-C6 level is OVERTURNED, and this level is APPROVED.

IV. CLINICAL ANALYSIS: C6-C7 LEVEL (UPHELD / DENIED)
The request for ACDF at the C6-C7 level does not meet the plan's clinical coverage criteria or generally accepted standards of medical practice:

1. Imaging and Symptom Mismatch (CC-SPINE-2024 Section 2.3 & Section 3.3): Section 2.3 requires that current imaging demonstrate structural pathology consistent with the member's symptoms and the proposed surgical level. Section 3.3 mandates denial when imaging does not demonstrate pathology at the proposed surgical level consistent with the clinical presentation. The MRI dated September 1, 2024, shows only a "mild disc bulge" and "minimal foraminal narrowing" at C6-C7, with "no cord contact" and "no nerve root compression identifiable." There are no documented C7 radicular symptoms (such as pain, numbness, or weakness in a C7 distribution) or correlating neurological deficits on exam.
2. Prophylactic Fusion and Medical Necessity (CHSC § 1374.32(a)): Dr. Wilson's clinical rationale for fusing the C6-C7 level is prophylactic stabilization to prevent adjacent segment disease. Under California's statutory definition of medical necessity (CHSC § 1374.32(a)), health care services must be clinically appropriate and "not primarily for the convenience of the patient, treating physician, or other provider." Generally accepted clinical standards, including the AANS/CNS Joint Guidelines (2023) and NASS Guidelines (2020), do not support prophylactic fusion of an asymptomatic adjacent level with minimal degenerative changes. Fusing an asymptomatic level solely to prevent potential future adjacent segment disease does not meet the threshold of medical necessity. Under Section 3.1 (Tier 3) of the Clinical Reference Summary, surgical intervention is "not indicated" for imaging findings without correlating symptoms.

Because there is no correlating clinical pathology or symptomatology at C6-C7, and prophylactic fusion does not meet the standard of medical necessity, the denial of the C6-C7 level is UPHELD.

V. SUMMARY OF AUTHORIZATION STATUS
- CPT Code 22551 (Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, first level): APPROVED for C5-C6.
- CPT Code 22551 / 22552 (Anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, second level): DENIED for C6-C7.

VI. NOTICE OF INDEPENDENT MEDICAL REVIEW (IMR) RIGHTS
Because a portion of your appeal has been denied, you have the right to request an Independent Medical Review (IMR) from the California Department of Managed Health Care (DMHC) under California Health & Safety Code § 1374.30.

The IMR process is a free, independent review conducted by medical professionals who are not affiliated with HealthFirst. You may apply for an IMR if the plan's decision has been upheld, modified, or delayed, and you believe the decision was incorrect.

To apply for an IMR:
1. Complete the IMR Application Form provided with this letter or apply online at the DMHC website (www.dmhc.ca.gov).
2. Submit your application within six (6) months of the date of this determination letter.
3. You may contact the DMHC Help Center at 1-888-466-2219 for assistance.

Sincerely,

Appeals and Grievances Department
HealthFirst Health Plan

ground_truth_answer: PARTIAL — OVERTURN for C5-C6 (criteria met, symptoms documented, imaging correlation confirmed). UPHOLD for C6-C7 (no documented C7 symptoms, minimal imaging findings, prophylactic fusion alone does not meet medical necessity standard). Correct answer is PARTIAL, not full OVERTURN.
genuine_tension: Plan criteria clearly met for the overall procedure. A single-pass system reads criteria met and OVERTURNs both levels. But the plan denied the C6-C7 level specifically because there are no symptoms and minimal imaging findings at that level. Clinical standards require symptom-imaging correlation for each fused level. The surgeon's prophylactic argument doesn't meet the medical necessity threshold for the second level.
